summary: Missing pro-rated buffer credit after deduplication of replayed postbacks
description:
Issue summary:
LexaHealth reports their finalized March invoice is missing a pro-rated hourly buffer credit that normally applies during fallback warmup windows when postbacks are deduplicated. The customer saw a negative line item of -$1,420 that they expect to be offset by a prorated buffer credit (~$1,350) for two multi-region warmup windows.

Impact:
- Customer reports unexpected charge and potential compliance review for overage (enterprise contract).
- Billing contact escalated to enterprise CS and finance.

Environment:
- Private deployment with hosted fallback enabled for eu-west to us-east routing.
- Customer uses reserved Dedicated pool with periodic private->hosted fallback during maintenance windows.

Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1. Schedule a batch embed job across eu-west at 02:00 UTC with reserved hours active.
2. During rollout, private connector briefly lost reachable nodes and requests fell back to hosted for ~18 minutes.
3. Postback replay/dedup process later consolidated multiple produced postbacks into single accepted postback (dedupe TTL/merge).
4. Final invoice line shows warmup/reserve buffer un-applied for that window.

Logs / Evidence provided by customer:
- Invoice PDF page 3 (attached) showing negative line -$1,420 and no buffer credit line.
- Postback audit IDs: pb_21f3a, pb_21f3b, pb_21f3c.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Emma Zhao (Support): Acknowledged receipt and opened request with billing ops. Asked for relevant invoice PDF and postback IDs. Notified finance and assigned to Mateo.
2026-03-10 - Mateo Ruiz (Support): Retrieved postback logs and initial reconciler trace. Confirmed dedupe events around 2026-03-02T02:15:00Z. Escalated to billing-engineer channel #billing-ops.

2026-03-11 - Priya Nair (Billing Ops): Observed that the hourly-buffer tag was present but its rate-label did not map to the customer's negotiated eco-rate due to a tag-normalizer change deployed 2026-02-28. Created INT-4821 to track patch for tag-normalizer rollback in staging.
2026-03-11 - Mateo Ruiz (Support): Informed customer that we have a provisional adjustment planned pending invoice reissue. Requested permission to issue credit memo or manual adjustment.
2026-03-12 - LexaHealth Billing (Customer): Approved provisional credit memo and requested confirmation once posted to their accounting system.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: Deduped postbacks were collapsed and the reconciler emitted a single usage event lacking the hourly-buffer metadata key required for pro-rate calculation.

Found a related deploy on 2026-02-28 to the tag-normalizer that introduced a corner-case: when postbacks are merged, the tag-normalizer preferred the first-seen rate_label, which for multi-region fallbacks can be empty for hosted-fallback events.

Reconciler trace (recon-logs-2026-03-02T02:15): user_lexa: three postbacks merged -> usage event u_99832 created without buffer_tag. Billing-rate-lookup attempted eco-rate fallback and returned default hosted tariff, which produced an unapplied buffer credit mismatch during invoice finalization.
Currency conversion: customer invoices in EUR with live conversion on finalization; rounding amplified delta from expected ~70 EUR to ~78 EUR due to sequence of rate-lookup vs conversion timing.
resolution_notes: Provisional resolution: Finance will issue a credit memo for the missing pro-rated buffer credit (credit memo CM-2026-0312-LEXA for €1,360). Billing-engineer patch PR merged to revert the tag-normalizer preference for merged postbacks (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/postback-reconciler/pull/287). Scheduled re-run of the reconciler for March 2 window to regenerate corrected usage events before next billing cycle close. Follow-ups: INT-4821 (tag-normalizer rollback), INT-4902 (reconciler re-run playbook). Notified customer of expected posting date 2026-03-14.
